## ❌ RuleHawk firewall gate **FAIL** — 8 finding(s) at or above `high` block this change. Rule-layer audit: routing, NAT and topology are not evaluated. | Score | Files | Rules | Critical | High | Medium | Low | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 0/100 | 1 | 10 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 1 | ### Segmentation violations A declared zone boundary is breached. Each row is a concrete packet the config **permits** that it must not: | Witness packet | Where | Fix | |---|---|---| | `10.20.0.1 -> 10.10.0.1:445 (tcp)` | `samples/ios_acl.txt:10` | deny 10.20.0.0/16 -> 10.10.0.0/16 port 445 before rule 8 (line 10) | | `203.0.113.1 -> 10.10.0.1 (ip)` | `samples/ios_acl.txt:11` | deny 203.0.113.0/24 -> 10.10.0.0/16 before rule 9 (line 11) | > **Next:** RuleHawk proved the rules permit a flow your policy forbids. Whether that packet is actually delivered across routing and NAT, and what tightening the rule breaks elsewhere, needs a forwarding model. Batfish is an open-source one.
❌ samples/ios_acl.txt (ios-asa, 10 rules, score 0/100, 9 finding(s)) - **CRITICAL** **segmentation-violation** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:10`) `permit tcp any any eq 445` SEGMENTATION VIOLATION (CORP must not reach PCI): the ACL PERMITS 10.20.0.1 -> 10.10.0.1:445 (tcp) via rule 8. witness: `10.20.0.1 -> 10.10.0.1:445 (tcp)` fix: _deny 10.20.0.0/16 -> 10.10.0.0/16 port 445 before rule 8 (line 10)_ - **CRITICAL** **permit-any-any** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:11`) `permit ip any any` permit ip any any — allows ALL traffic; defeats the ACL. fix: _replace with least-privilege permits + a default deny_ - **CRITICAL** **segmentation-violation** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:11`) `permit ip any any` SEGMENTATION VIOLATION (DMZ must not reach PCI): the ACL PERMITS 203.0.113.1 -> 10.10.0.1 (ip) via rule 9. witness: `203.0.113.1 -> 10.10.0.1 (ip)` fix: _deny 203.0.113.0/24 -> 10.10.0.0/16 before rule 9 (line 11)_ - **CRITICAL** **intent-inversion-deny-dead** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:12`) `deny tcp any any eq 22` This deny NEVER takes effect — an earlier permit (rule 9) already allows the same traffic. The traffic you meant to block is ALLOWED. cause: permit ip any any fix: _move rule 10 (line 12) above rule 9 (line 11)_ - **HIGH** **intent-inversion-permit-dead** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:5`) `permit tcp 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 host 203.0.113.10 eq 23` This permit NEVER takes effect — an earlier deny (rule 2) already drops the same traffic. Likely a silent connectivity loss. cause: deny tcp 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 any eq 23 fix: _move rule 3 (line 5) above rule 2 (line 4), or narrow rule 2_ - **HIGH** **dangerous-exposure** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:6`) `permit tcp any any eq 3389` Sensitive service(s) permitted from ANY source: rdp. fix: _restrict the source, or remove if unused_ - **HIGH** **intent-inversion-permit-dead** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:9`) `permit ip 192.168.5.0 0.0.0.255 any` This permit NEVER takes effect — an earlier deny (rule 6) already drops the same traffic. Likely a silent connectivity loss. cause: deny ip 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255 any fix: _move rule 7 (line 9) above rule 6 (line 8), or narrow rule 6_ - **HIGH** **dangerous-exposure** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:10`) `permit tcp any any eq 445` Sensitive service(s) permitted from ANY source: smb. fix: _restrict the source, or remove if unused_ - **LOW** **redundant** (`samples/ios_acl.txt:7`) `permit tcp host 198.51.100.5 host 203.0.113.10 eq 443` Rule is redundant — fully covered by an earlier permit (rule 1); safe to remove. cause: permit tcp any host 203.0.113.10 eq 443 fix: _remove rule 5 (line 7)_
RuleHawk runs entirely inside your runner — your config never leaves your infrastructure. · [docs](https://github.com/optimesh-ai/RuleHawk)
